purpose: automate the mechanics of releasing so deployments are fast, consistent and low-risk
entry_criteria: Deployment procedure is written and has been done by hand successfully
Target environment is defined as code
procedure: Convert each manual step into a scripted, idempotent step with clear success and failure output.
Add pre-checks: the right artifact digest, healthy targets, free capacity, no active incident.
Use a progressive strategy (rolling, canary or blue-green) with automated health gates between stages.
Make rollback one automated action that restores the previous version and configuration.
Run the automation in staging repeatedly, including a forced failure, before using it in production.
Document how to run, stop and debug it.
acceptance_criteria: A forced failure was handled correctly in staging
validation_method: Release engineering review and rehearsal evidence.

validation.command: ./deploy.sh --env staging --digest sha256:<digest> && ./deploy.sh --env staging --digest sha256:<digest>   # example: run twice
validation.expect: second run makes no change and succeeds

validation.check: inject a failing health check in staging and run the deployment

failure_modes.response: Make each step safe to repeat
Remove the bypass or require approval

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A canary deployment script sends five percent of traffic to the new version, checks error rate for ten minutes, then continues or rolls back automatically; a staging rehearsal with a failing check shows the rollback working.
